copies.headline: CJ's Receivers Can't Cover Adam's Spread
copies.body:
The receiver room decides this one. Adam's top three — Jaxon Smith-Njigba against a Raiders defense Seattle should carve up, Chris Olave in a 48.5-total divisional game, Jalen Coker — project 49 to CJ's 38, and CJ's depth behind that is Devaughn Vele and an Emeka Egbuka goose egg. Parker Washington's 14 leans on Jacksonville being favored by 10.5 in Tennessee, which is exactly the script where the Jaguars run clock and the slot receiver disappears. Rashee Rice and DK Metcalf are fine, not fixes. Adam adds Brock Purdy in a 55.5-total game at Dallas, the highest number on the board, plus Sam LaPorta.
CJ's one real edge is the backfield, where Chuba Hubbard and Jonathan Taylor top Kenneth Walker and Rico Dowdle by two — but Taylor's game has a 38.5 total and Indy may just sit on Miami. Tyler Shough is a leaky floor at quarterback with Watson out. Adam leads the league at 143.1 a game and just put up 170.8; CJ hasn't cleared 108 in three weeks.

copies.headline: Kaleb's Luck Meets Logan's Actual Roster
copies.body:
Logan leads at every position on the top-options read — plus-2 at quarterback, plus-4 at running back, plus-7 at receiver — and the schedule underneath it is friendlier. Joe Burrow gets Pittsburgh in a 49.5 game, Tetairoa McMillan is in the week's best shootout environment at New Orleans, and Jaylen Warren and Germie Bernard both come from that same Bengals-Steelers total. Justin Jefferson in a 42.5 at Green Bay is the one soft spot, and Xavier Worthy and Rashid Shaheed being questionable means the WR3 slot could wobble. But 123.3 per game, 4th in scoring, a 63-36 all-play, and minus-1.7 luck wins says this is a top-four roster that's been getting robbed.
Kaleb is 5-4 because the schedule gift-wrapped it. He's last in points at 100.5, last in all-play at 34-65, and has posted 62.7 and 76.8 the past two weeks. The receiver room is wide and shallow — Drake London at 15 is the only real anchor, McConkey and Carnell Tate are questionable, and Wicks is out. Ashton Jeanty draws Seattle in a 40.5, and Breece Hall is on an 8.5-point dog, which at least means late volume. Jared Goff in a 51.5 against New England is the one genuine ceiling play, but one good game script doesn't close a 15-point positional gap.

copies.headline: Noah's Receiver Room Is A Rumor
copies.body:
The quarterbacks and backfields wash — Trevor Lawrence and Drake Maye both project 22, and Christian's Bhayshul Tuten/Chase Brown pairing matches James Cook at 31 — so this comes down to the two spots where Noah has nothing. Christian's top three receivers (CeeDee Lamb, Jameson Williams, Khalil Shakir, with a questionable Deebo Samuel in reserve) beat Noah's best three by 14, and George Kittle over Hunter Henry is another six. That's a 20-point hole before anyone touches a ball, and Noah's WR depth chart reads Garrett Wilson (questionable), Josh Downs, Jordyn Tyson. Jaylen Waddle is tagged too. There's no fourth option to cover a scratch.
Christian's points also come from better games. Lamb is in a 55.5-total Cowboys-49ers track meet with Kittle on the other sideline, and Lawrence is a 10.5-point favorite who may spend the fourth quarter handing off to Tuten. Noah's path is Maye chasing in Detroit at 51.5 and Cook volume against the Jets. Live, but thin. Christian is scoring 124.7 a game, third in the league, and is 4-5 only because the schedule has robbed him of 1.4 wins. This is the correction.

copies.headline: Leif's Backfield Outruns John's Tight End Hoard
copies.body:
Leif has the better roster and the worse résumé: 6-3 with a 45-54 all-play and three straight weeks under 96. The edge here is the ground game. McCaffrey (22) in a 55.5-total game at Dallas and Henry (18) against a Chargers defense in a 38.5-total grinder give Leif 40 at running back to John's 30, and if David Montgomery's questionable tag clears, Woody Marks at 14 is a flex most teams can't match. Josh Allen adds seven over Stafford, with Buffalo laying 8.5 in the week's second-biggest total.
The receiver room is the ugly part. Adams is on IR, Mike Evans and Omar Cooper are questionable, Sutton projects zero — Leif is one inactive from starting Marvin Harrison Jr. at 6 and liking it. John counters with Bowers and McBride, a real six-point tight end edge, but Nacua doubtful leaves DeMario Douglas as his WR1. That's not enough volume to cover the backfield gap.

copies.headline: Mitchell's Backfield Buys Back Some Dignity
copies.body:
The math is a backfield story. Mitchell's top two runners project 35 to Isaac's 27, and that gap is wider than it looks because Isaac's RB room is a wreck — Cam Skattebo out, Saquon Barkley and J.K. Dobbins on bye, leaving Javonte Williams alone in a Dallas-San Francisco game with a 55.5 total, the best shootout environment on the slate. Jahmyr Gibbs gets Detroit as a home favorite in a 51.5-point game, and Rachaad White and Jordan Mason are real bodies, not thoughts and prayers. Isaac claws back at receiver, where Ja'Marr Chase and Malik Nabers project 39 between them.
That's the ceiling question: Isaac needs Chase to actually produce against Pittsburgh. Mitchell's spread is flatter — Matthew Golden in a 42.5-total slog, DJ Moore in Buffalo's blowout script, Nico Collins in a 40.5-total game at Cleveland. Quarterback and tight end are a wash. Isaac is 5-4 on luck he hasn't earned; the all-play records, 38 percent to 41 percent, say these are the same bad team.

copies.headline: Peter's Receiver Room Is Held Together With Tape
copies.body:
Grant wins this at wide receiver and it isn't close. Amon-Ra St. Brown in a 51.5-total game against New England, Christian Watson in Green Bay's 42.5 with Minnesota chasing, and Zay Flowers as the only real Baltimore target make 51 projected points off three names. Peter counters with Tee Higgins in the week's best environment — Cincinnati-Pittsburgh at 49.5 — and then a pile of question marks: Denzel Boston, George Pickens and A.J. Brown all carry tags, and Brown is projected at zero. Adonai Mitchell gets volume as the Jets trail Buffalo by 8.5, but that's a dart, not a plan.
Peter's edge is Bijan Robinson against Kansas City, and with Jacobs and Monangai out, Audric Estime is the entire RB2. Grant's four-back rotation is unspectacular but functional. Mahomes questionable is the one lever that flips this; Geno Smith in a 50.5 shootout is a soft landing. Peter is 5-4 on luck — all-play 41-58 says the bill comes due.

intro: Leif at John is the one worth watching: the Engen-Lundquist matchup carries real seeding weight with Leif a game back of Adam and John clinging to the back half of the bye picture, and it's the only game on the board where both rosters are running out full-strength backfields. The ugliest spot is Mitchell at Isaac — Mitchell is somehow favored at 2-7, which tells you everything about the week Isaac's lineup is walking into with the byes gutting his flex. Elsewhere, Grant is favored at home over Peter, which would drop the Lundquist brothers to a combined 1-1 on the day and give Peter something to think about at Thanksgiving.
